domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Given positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and given an integer n greater than 1 that is congruent to 1 modulo 2d, it follows that n is odd, gcd(d,n)=1, r times (1 minus n) divided by 2 is an integer, and for every integer k between 0 and n inclusive, k times (d minus d times k minus 2r) divided by 2 is an integer.
quantifier_order: For all positive integers d and r, with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d
For all integers n greater than 1 such that n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d
For every integer k with 0 <= k <= n

variables.domain: integers greater than 1 and congruent to 1 modulo 2d
variables.name: n
k
variables.role: universally quantified index in the final claim

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses appear; the statement is purely universal after fixing d, r, and n.
The integrality of r times (1 minus n) divided by 2 depends on the derived fact that n is odd.
The integrality of k times (d minus d times k minus 2r) divided by 2 is asserted separately for each admissible k and does not rely on an auxiliary witness.

statement_nl: Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and let n > 1 satisfy n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Then n is odd, gcd(d,n)=1, the integer r(1-n)/2 is an integer, and for every integer k with 0 <= k <= n one has k(d-dk-2r)/2 ∈ Z.
